title: Practised Hands
logline: At a festival-night stall handing out free food to strangers, one volunteer's hands move without a single wasted motion after twenty years; beside them, someone doing it for the first time can barely look a stranger in the eye.
human_question: Does kindness get easier, or does it just start to look different once you've done it enough times?

premise.story: One long night at a volunteer-run free food or drinks stall during a local festival, following an experienced volunteer and a first-timer side by side.
premise.place: A roadside stall during a temple festival, strings of lights, a long night of strangers passing through.
premise.experience: The contrast between practised ease and first-time shyness, doing exactly the same task.

concept_links.why: Proficiency (pāguññatā) makes practised giving easy and even sweet, while its absence brings hesitation, fear and shame at doing it for the first time [C023-P:L153-L157].
Both the confident and the hesitant act are counted as fully wholesome; the sources never treat prompted or unpractised giving as less real [C011-P:L93-L109].

what_camera_could_observe: The stall being set up before the crowd arrives
The queue and the rhythm of serving, hour after hour
The experienced volunteer's economical, unhesitating movements
The newcomer's hesitation, and how it changes, if it does, by the end of the night
what_must_be_real: Real volunteers giving up a real night of their own time. No staged nerves or arranged 'first-timer' performance.

possible_arc.opening: The stall going up before the crowd.
possible_arc.turn: The newcomer's uncertain first hour, beside the practised volunteer's ease.
possible_arc.ending_open: However the night actually ends, and whatever the two volunteers say to each other, if anything.

requirements: A genuine volunteer-run free food or drinks stall at an actual festival
At least one long-serving volunteer and one real first-time volunteer, both willing to be filmed
Permission from event organisers for overnight filming

suggestions.name: A town temple festival
suggestions.region: Southern Province (e.g. Matara or Tangalle area)
suggestions.why: Local temple festivals across the south regularly involve volunteer-run free food and drink stalls.
suggestions.verify: No specific festival, stall or volunteers have been identified or confirmed.

risks: Performative generosity staged for the camera
Treating recipients as background rather than people with their own dignity
drop_if: No genuine first-time volunteer can be found, or the event turns out to be organised specifically for filming

connections.note: Both watch the same kind of giving become easier, or simply different, with repetition over time.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
